Compatibility

  • Works with Mariner, Daytona Small Stature, Malibu, Newport and Coral systems.
  • Implants are titanium alloy or cobalt chrome — axial and parallel connectors in different shapes and rod slots, plus rods.
  • Fits rods from Ø4.5mm to Ø6.35mm (Ti and/or CoCr).

System features

  • Versatile implant offering for both 5.5 and 6.0 rod combinations
  • Implants designed to accommodate challenging anatomies
  • Intuitive instrumentation for improved surgical flow and OR efficiency
  • Revision implants with variability to help with augmenting spinal fusion constructs

Pre-operative planning

  • Know the Outrigger system offering
  • Lateral and A/P fluoroscopy helps decide the approach and which implants suit
  • Know the existing hardware
Indications & contraindications
Indications

Immobilisation and stabilisation of spinal segments in skeletally mature patients as an adjunct to fusion, as a pedicle screw fixation system (T1–S2/ilium), for: degenerative disc disease, spondylolisthesis, trauma, spinal stenosis, deformities (scoliosis, kyphosis, lordosis), tumour, pseudarthrosis (failed previous fusion). Used with autograft or allograft.

With the Daytona Small Stature system in paediatric patients: also AIS, neuromuscular and congenital scoliosis (posterior approach only).

Absolute contraindications
  • Infection in or around the operative site
  • Allergy or sensitivity to implant materials
  • Any case not described in the indications
Relative contraindications
  • Local inflammation; fever or leukocytosis
  • Morbid obesity; pregnancy
  • Grossly distorted anatomy
  • Metabolic bone disease, osteopenia / osteoporosis
  • Raised ESR or WBC unexplained by other disease, or marked left shift
  • Inadequate tissue coverage over the site
  • Skeletally immature patient
  • Patient unwilling to follow post-op instructions
  • Use with other devices with incompatible materials

Not exhaustive — see full instructions for use.

1

Surgical approach

Patient prone. Identify the surgical site with fluoroscopy, then make the appropriate incision to reach the desired anatomical location.

2

Site preparation

Clear bone and fusion mass so the Outrigger implant can sit on the existing rod.

Box chisel — angled / straight

Removes bone; helps gain access to the previously implanted rod.

C-chisel — angled / straight

Removes previous fusion mass away from the implanted rod, giving clearance to place the implant onto the existing construct.

InstrumentRun-on-rodTip past 5.5 rodTip past 6.0 rod
Box cutter9mmup to 5mmup to 4.5mm
C-chisel9mmup to 2mmup to 1.5mm
Rasp

Removes remaining fusion material from below the previous rods. Place it over the existing rod and rotate axially to engage the cutting features.

NOTECutting features are distal and circumferential.
Rongeur

Removes previous fusion mass from above or below the existing construct using its distal cutting features.

NOTECutting features are distal only.
3

Implant placement

Side / closed implants

T-25 Tapered Inserter (pre-loaded into the aqua set screw) places the implant onto the existing rod; provisionally tighten to the rod.

The Implant Holder works with any implant that has notches: compress the handle so the distal feature mates with the notches. To release, press the trigger at the proximal end of the handle and remove.

NOTEThe Implant Inserter interfaces with the notches on the implants to hold them securely.
Top-loading (gold) implants

The Top-loading Implant Inserter threads directly into any top-loading Outrigger implant for a secure hold.

4

Implant tightening

T-25 Torque Driver for aqua set screws, or T-30 Torque Driver for gold set screws — with the Torque Limiting T-handle and the correct-size Counter Torque. Turn the T-handle clockwise until the audible click to reach the final torque of 85 in/lb.

Counter torque shafts

Four modular shafts are in the set — each mates with an implant based on the width of the implant (8, 10, 16 and 20mm).

5

Implant removal

Put the T-25 Torque Driver into the aqua set screw, or the T-30 Torque Driver into the gold set screw, and turn counter-clockwise to loosen the implant.
